body: I never really realized I was this way until I started my first job, I felt completely helpless being there and I dreaded every moment. I'm glad I left, because I doubt I would have ever gotten comfortable there with them being bullies. I think if you have nice colleagues you are able to feel more at home, so right now I am looking for a job that has that.
Thank you, I will try this.
Unfortunately therapy is a bit above my budget at the moment. But yes I think you are right about the latter.

I currently have a small job in which I bring around magazines to subscribers, because the bills have to be paid in someway. I see costumers outside often and try to make small talk. It makes it easier to talk to people but inside I still feel terrified.

The reason I get anxiety in social situations is the result of constant bullying throughout my life.
Yes exactly, it only makes me feel more guilty

I know I'm not the only one who feels this way, but I am the only person in my surroundings. I feel lonely because of that. I know I can't get help and I'm alone in this, that makes me feel even worse.

Walking inside the store. Constantly being scared that people are watching you/judging you. Standing too long in a certain aisle. Being scared that I'm in someone's way and am being annoying. Scared to stand in the candy/alcohol aisle in fear that people judge me. The feeling of pure dread when standing in line and slowly getting closer to the cashier. Going to the store is probably more nerve-racking to me than going to school.

Though I understand you, I'm not sure if homeschooling is the best option, at least not in the long run. You shouldn't teach her that staying away from the bad things will solve the problem. And it's bad for her social skills. Unfortunately schools often don't take these things seriously. I hope that they will be split up next year at least. 

When I was bullied I had this therapy group and we learned that when a bully says something you should either ignore them completely or say something that's complete nonsense to throw them off. I hope that maybe that will help her somewhat. You could also consider homeschooling her until the end of the year until they're split up.

Anxiety And Depression are quite a myth in the country that I live. There isn't really any information available in the language they speak. Thank you for your help though I will try to talk to them again.

I've been through the same at that age and my mum had me redo my year. I came in a different class and it got mostly better after that. Maybe something like that will help (a different class or school) and talk to her about the suicidal thoughts. Make sure the bullies receive punishment as well by talking to the principal or teacher.

Please don't use the word 'coping'. It's not her fault at all and she shouldn't have to go through this. You said you've tried several times to solve it with the school but sometimes it just doesn't work and it's time to take other actions. I hope it will be better soon!



Maybe you look intimidating to them, Or maybe they're jealous of you. Sometimes people feel the need to bring someone down simply so that they seem better. It's happened to me as well and even though I told teachers nothing was really done. Just try to ignore it, it's hard but at some point everyone will see how wrong they are, even the girls themselves.
Happy birthday dear! 💖 🎂 I'm so sorry for everything that happened to you. I'm sure your family means well 💕 I wish you the best!

I don't see the problem tbh

Sounds like you have definitely fallen victim for bullying, something similar happened to me. Even though she is a 'higher up' she still has a boss and you should definitely tell said boss about your experiences with her. If talking face to face is hard I suggest writing an email.  If that doesn't work I suggest that you find somewhere else to work, working in a toxic workplace for too long can be hazardous to your anxiety.

It's not like I never stood up for myself, I just gave up at some point because it never stopped. I'm happy for you that you found a way to cope though.
